items.event_time_ist: Tuesday night, Oct 13, 2026 (Saudi local time); Reuters damage assessment published Wednesday, Oct 14, 2026
items.summary: Three people with direct knowledge told Reuters that Aramco's Dhahran headquarters suffered 'extensive damage' in Tuesday night's Houthi strike: a fire started on the 9th floor of the south wing, spread across floors 6-10, and the top three floors - where CEO Amin Nasser's office sits - were severely damaged, with part of the ceiling caved in and windows and doors blown out. The fire was still burning into the early hours of Wednesday. Some employees were asked to work from home and some functions shifted to global offices, though operations continued normally. This directly contradicts the Energy Ministry's 'limited fire' framing; AP separately confirmed the CEO's office was hit. The complex hosts the operations center overseeing Aramco's rigs, refineries, export terminals and pipelines. Aramco did not comment.
items.title: Reuters: sources say Aramco Dhahran HQ suffered 'extensive damage' in Tuesday-night strike; staff sent home, functions shifted abroad

items.summary: Brent crude futures rose ~0.8% to $106.58 a barrel by 0030 GMT Wednesday and later traded around $106.2 (+0.5%), with WTI at ~$94.7-94.9, as traders weighed supply risk from the Houthi-Saudi fighting against prospects of more Russian diesel. A Nissan Securities strategist told Reuters that 'supply concern stemming from conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia is driving prices higher.' The move follows Tuesday night's strike on Aramco's Dhahran HQ and the week's attacks on Saudi airports and energy sites.
items.title: Brent crude ~$106/barrel Wednesday as traders price Houthi-Saudi supply risk
